scenario.description: A lead technology counsel must decide whether to approve the public release of an internal machine-learning toolkit and set the licensing, scope, export, and data-cleansing conditions, with input from open-source, commercial, export-control, and privacy counsel.

shared_context.S1: The engineering team plans to publish the Atlas machine-learning toolkit in the company's public repository next Friday.
shared_context.S2: The toolkit is intended for external developers and includes source code, documentation, and a sample training package.
shared_context.S3: Elena Marquez gives the final legal approval for the public release and records any conditions in the release ticket.
shared_context.S4: The firm's weekly product-release legal gate includes a checklist update from open-source, commercial, export-control, and privacy counsel before the final approval is recorded.
shared_context.S5: Elena records approval only after all pre-release conditions have been completed and documented; if any condition remains outstanding, the release approval must be recorded as false, and detailed remediation planning is handled after that decision.

PF1.text: While reviewing the build manifest this week, Noah confirmed that the public distribution links the toolkit with a GPLv3 library, so the combined distribution must use the GPLv3 license and include corresponding source and attribution notices; he has not updated the release ticket.

PF2.text: Maya reviewed the largest customer's source-code agreement and confirmed that the customer's proprietary connector is included in the current build; the agreement prohibits public release of that connector without written customer consent, so the public package must exclude the connector, be limited to the core toolkit, and document the exclusion in the release checklist; she has not added this contract restriction to the release checklist.

PF3.text: Owen confirmed with the export-classification team this week that Atlas contains covered encryption functionality and requires a SNAP-R self-classification filing before public release; completion of the filing must be documented in the release ticket, and the classification confirmation is in his working file but not in the release ticket.

PF4.text: Sofia's review of the sample training package found exactly 312 pseudonymized customer records; privacy approval requires removing all 312 records and documenting the removal before any public release, and she has not yet entered that gate in the product checklist.

acceptance_conditions: The release must not be approved until all listed legal conditions are recorded.
The combined distribution must use GPLv3.
The public scope must be recorded exactly as core_toolkit_only.
The customer proprietary connector must be excluded.
A SNAP-R self-classification filing must be completed before release.
Exactly 312 training records must be removed before release.
The release must include source and attribution notices.
The exclusion of the customer proprietary connector must be documented in the release checklist.
The completion of the SNAP-R filing must be documented in the release ticket.
The privacy removal must be documented before release.

content_checks.C7: any('source' in c['detail'] and 'attribution' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: any('connector' in c['detail'] and ('exclude' in c['detail'] or 'exclusion' in c['detail']) and ('document' in c['detail'] or 'checklist' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)
content_checks.C9: any('document' in c['detail'] and 'SNAP-R' in c['detail'] and 'filing' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C10: any('document' in c['detail'] and '312' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The build manifest changes the license decision to GPLv3 and requires the commitment to include source and attribution notices.
The customer agreement changes the public scope to exactly core_toolkit_only, requires the connector to be excluded, and requires documenting that exclusion.
The export classification changes the pre-release condition to completion of a SNAP-R self-classification filing and documentation of that filing.
The privacy review changes the training-package condition to removal of exactly 312 records and documentation of that removal.
